note: Blank template. No personal records are used in this project. Fill this in yourself if you want a personal evidence ledger in your own copy; leave it empty otherwise.
reflection_questions: Think of the last time you had to work out what someone actually needed, as opposed to what they first asked for. What did you do to find out, and did you enjoy that part or only the result?
Name one task you have done repeatedly for weeks. Did your interest hold once it stopped being new? What kept it or lost it?
When you last prepared thoroughly for something that then did not happen or was rejected, how did you react over the following week?
Have you ever had to tell someone something they did not want to hear when staying quiet would have been easier? What did you say, and would you do it the same way again?
Which do you reach for first when you have a free hour with a new topic: the numbers, the people involved, or the mechanism? Give a real recent example.
Describe a time you were responsible for someone else's deadline or deliverable without having authority over them. What was satisfying and what was draining?
What have you learned about investments or markets without being asked to? How far did you take it before stopping, and why did you stop?
When you have been measured against a target, did the target change how you treated the people involved? How do you know?
Which would bother you more: being wrong in front of a client, or being slow? What real episode makes you think so?
If this role had the same work and pay at a firm nobody had heard of, what would you lose that you care about? Be specific.
What would you need to see in the first six months to conclude this career is not for you?
Which adjacent role (research, portfolio management, consulting, private wealth, banking) have you actually tested, and what did the test show?
